I need to decide whether to buy or auction the property at ILLINOIS_AVENUE.

I have $1035 cash and own Vermont Avenue and Water Works. I need to decide whether to buy the $240 Red property or auction it.

Opponent p1 owns three railroads and two of three pink and orange properties. Opponent p2 owns Mediterranean, B&O RR, Ventnor, and Pacific. The yellow and green groups are split between the two.

Opponent p4 owns North Carolina Avenue and has $1248. I have been saving cash to complete the light blue group, which remains open. The red group is split: Indiana is owned by p1, while Kentucky and Illinois are unowned.

I cannot complete the red group without acquiring Indiana from p1. Buying Illinois would leave me with $795, enough to purchase Oriental and Connecticut and build three houses on the light blue group.

Auctioning could secure the property for less or block another player from acquiring it. The main downside is that buying Illinois would abandon my light blue monopoly plan and force a trade with p1 for Indiana.

Auctioning would likely draw bids from p4 and p2, but p1 probably cannot afford a high bid. The standard strategy is to always buy Illinois Avenue if affordable, since it is the most landed-on property and reds are the strongest color group.

Denying Illinois to other players and holding it as a trade chip is valuable even without the full red set. The light blue-only strategy was too conservative. After the purchase, I would have $795 remaining, enough to buy Oriental and Connecticut and build houses on the light blue group.

Boardwalk and Park Place are also unowned properties I might land on. $795 would still cover Boardwalk after the purchase. Auctioning is risky because p1 especially wants Illinois, so opponents will likely bid near or above the list price.

I will buy Illinois Avenue. Auctioning it risks giving p1 a cheap second red property, which would complete their red group and threaten me. I will keep my public message brief and strategic.
